newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium to sell EU real estate in Maastricht drive.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to sell EU real estate in Maastricht drive.

text.p: Belgium plans to sell off real estate rented out to the European Union (EU) -- including a country club founded by European civil servants -- to help it qualify for economic and monetary union (EMU).
Among the other properties up for sale, according to notices published in Belgian newspapers this week, are European Parliament offices and parking places used by various EU institutions.
"It's part of the effort to reach the Maastricht criteria," an official involved in the sale told Reuters.

In presenting his 1997 budget to parliament on Tuesday, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said the government aimed to bring its deficit next year under the three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) required by the Maastricht Treaty.

The goal would be met through a combination of around 80 billion Belgian francs ($2.55 billion) of tax hikes and spending cuts and other one-off items, such as the sale of state assets, including property.
The properties being sold by the state include the "Van Maerlant" office complex, which is leased to the European Parliament until 2007 for 145 million Belgian francs a year.
The building houses offices for members of the parliament, meeting rooms, a restaurant and two bars.
Also included is a bridge across Brussels' Rue Belliard connecting the building to European Parliament offices owned by private Belgian real estate fund Cofinimmo.

The state is also selling the Chateau Saint Anne, a 19th century luxury villa on the edge of Brussels, complete with swimming pool and tennis courts. The chateau has, since 1968, been the home of a club founded with the government's help by European civil servants and Belgians in 1961.
The chateau, asking price a minimum 76 million francs, is adjacent to the Belgian government's own Val Duchesse country house, where the 1997 budget was prepared by top ministers.
The properties go under the hammer at a public auction on October 29. ($1=31.36 Belgian Franc)
